name: Reptile Heat Lamp Guard
short_description: A sturdy wire heat lamp guard that keeps reptiles from touching hot bulbs inside the enclosure. Fits most basking bulbs and ceramic heat emitters.
long_description:
A heat lamp guard is one of the most important safety items for any enclosure where a basking bulb or ceramic heat emitter is mounted inside. This reptile heat lamp guard is a sturdy, powder-coated wire cage that surrounds the bulb so climbing reptiles can't touch it, while still letting heat and light pass through. Contact burns from unguarded bulbs are one of the most common injuries vets see in pet reptiles, and a simple guard prevents them.

## Who needs a lamp guard

- **Climbing species** such as crested geckos, chameleons, tree boas and many monitors, which will climb straight onto a hot fixture.
- **PVC and wooden enclosures** where lamps are mounted inside the enclosure rather than over a mesh top.
- **Any setup with a ceramic heat emitter**, which can reach temperatures high enough to burn badly within seconds.

## Specifications

- **Size:** fits bulbs up to about 4.5 in (11.5 cm) in diameter and 6 in (15 cm) long, covering most halogen floods, ceramic heat emitters and deep heat projectors
- **Construction:** welded steel wire with a heat-resistant black powder coat
- **Mounting:** screw-mount base plate that attaches to the enclosure ceiling, with a ceramic socket (included) rated to 150 W
- **Spacing:** wide enough for efficient heat transfer, narrow enough to keep feet and tails out

## Installation tips

Mount the guard at the warm end of the enclosure, at least a few inches above the highest perch the animal can reach, so it can't lie on top of the cage. Fit your bulb, connect it to a thermostat and check the basking surface with an infrared thermometer. A [dimming thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/dimming-thermostat) suits light-emitting bulbs, while a [proportional thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/proportional-thermostat) suits ceramic heat emitters.

Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) has a full safety checklist for mounting heat sources inside enclosures.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a lamp guard if my bulb is above a mesh top?

Usually not, as long as the animal can't reach the mesh directly under the bulb for long periods. Guards are essential when bulbs are mounted inside the enclosure.

### Can I use a lamp guard with a ceramic heat emitter?

Yes. Ceramic heat emitters get extremely hot, so a guard is strongly recommended whenever one is mounted inside an enclosure.

### Does a lamp guard reduce heat output?

Very little. The wire spacing lets almost all heat and light through, though you may need to fine-tune your thermostat after fitting it.

name: Dual Dome Lamp Fixture – 2 × 5.5 in
short_description: A dual dome lamp fixture with two independently switched 5.5 in reflectors and ceramic sockets, for a wide basking area or bulbs side by side.
long_description:
A dual dome lamp fixture holds two bulbs side by side over a mesh top, giving you a wider, more even basking area than a single lamp. This dual dome lamp fixture has two 5.5 in deep reflectors on one bar, each with its own ceramic socket rated to 100 W and its own on/off switch. It is a long-time favorite of bearded dragon and uromastyx keepers, who use two smaller halogen bulbs to warm the whole body instead of one small hot spot.

## Why use two bulbs

- **Wider basking zone:** two bulbs side by side heat the full length of a lizard's body.
- **More even surface temperatures:** fewer hot spots than one high-wattage bulb.
- **Flexibility:** pair two halogens, or a halogen with a ceramic heat emitter for night heat on a separate circuit.
- **Backup:** if one bulb fails, the other keeps some heat going until you replace it.

## Specifications

- **Reflectors:** two 5.5 in (14 cm) deep aluminum domes
- **Sockets:** ceramic E26, each rated up to 100 W
- **Controls:** independent switches and separate cords, so each bulb can go to its own thermostat
- **Mounting:** rests on mesh tops with heat-resistant feet, or hangs from a lamp stand

## How to use it

Place the fixture over the basking platform at the warm end of the enclosure. Fit two [50 W halogen basking bulbs](/shop/heating-lighting/halogen-basking-bulb-50w) for most bearded dragon setups, then connect both to a [dimming thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/dimming-thermostat) through a power strip, with the probe at the basking surface. Check the basking surface with an infrared thermometer and raise or lower the platform to reach 100–110°F (38–43°C) for adult dragons.

Our [bearded dragon care sheet](/blog/bearded-dragon-care-sheet) explains basking temperatures, and our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) covers thermostats and safe mounting.

## Frequently asked questions

### What bulbs can I use in a dual dome fixture?

Halogen and incandescent basking bulbs, ceramic heat emitters or deep heat projectors up to 100 W per socket. Don't exceed the socket rating.

### Can I put each bulb on a different thermostat?

Yes. Each dome has its own cord, so you can run a basking bulb on a dimming thermostat and a ceramic heat emitter on a separate thermostat for night heat.

### Is a dual dome good for bearded dragons?

Yes. Two bulbs side by side create a wide, even basking area, which suits bearded dragons particularly well.

name: Mercury Vapor Bulb – 100 W UVB & Heat
short_description: A 100 W self-ballasted mercury vapor bulb that provides UVB, UVA, visible light and heat from one lamp, for large basking reptiles.
long_description:
A mercury vapor bulb provides UVB, UVA, bright visible light and basking heat from a single lamp, which makes it popular for large enclosures, tortoise tables and outdoor-style setups. This 100 W self-ballasted mercury vapor bulb screws into a standard ceramic socket and produces a focused, sun-like basking zone for desert and full-sun species such as bearded dragons, tortoises and uromastyx.

## How mercury vapor bulbs differ

- **All-in-one:** UVB and heat from one bulb, so you need only one fixture over the basking spot.
- **Strong, focused output:** best for larger enclosures where the animal basks some distance from the lamp.
- **Can't be dimmed:** mercury vapor bulbs must not be used on a dimming or pulse thermostat, which can damage them. Control temperature by adjusting the bulb height or basking platform instead, or use an on/off thermostat only on the backup heat source.

## Specifications

- **Wattage:** 100 W
- **Base:** E26/E27, ceramic socket required
- **Output:** UVB, UVA, visible light and infrared heat
- **Recommended distance:** basking surface roughly 12–18 in (30–45 cm) below the bulb, depending on mesh and species
- **Lifespan:** replace about every 12 months; UVB output declines before the light dims

## Installation tips

Use a deep dome fixture with a ceramic socket, mounted vertically over the basking spot. Run the bulb on a timer, not a thermostat. Measure the basking surface with an infrared thermometer and, ideally, the UV index with a UV meter, then adjust the height until both are in range. For bearded dragons, aim for a basking surface of 100–110°F (38–43°C).

If you need precise temperature control, many keepers prefer a separate T5 HO UVB tube plus a halogen basking bulb on a dimming thermostat. Our [UVB lighting guide](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained) compares the options, and our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) covers safe mounting.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I put a mercury vapor bulb on a thermostat?

Not on a dimming or pulse-proportional thermostat. These bulbs need full, steady power. Control temperature by adjusting the bulb height or basking platform instead.

### How long does a mercury vapor bulb last?

Most keepers replace them about every 12 months, because UVB output fades before the visible light does.

### Is a mercury vapor bulb good for tortoises?

Yes. It provides UVB and heat over a focused basking area, which suits tortoise tables and large open enclosures.

name: T5 HO UVB Lighting Kit – 22 in, 12% Desert
short_description: A complete UVB lighting kit: a 22 in T5 HO 12% desert tube in a slim reflector fixture with mounting clips, ready to install.
long_description:
This UVB lighting kit pairs a 22 in T5 HO 12% desert UVB tube with a slim, high-efficiency reflector fixture, so you get a correctly matched UVB setup in one box. T5 HO tubes are now widely regarded as the gold standard for UVB, and buying the tube and fixture together avoids the most common mistake: a strong tube in a fixture without a reflector, or a weak tube in a good fixture.

## Who it's for

The 22 in length suits 24–36 in long enclosures for desert and full-sun species, including juvenile bearded dragons, Rankin's dragons, uromastyx and many tortoises in smaller setups. For a 4 ft bearded dragon enclosure, our 34 in tube and fixture are a better fit.

## What's in the box

- **22 in T5 HO 12% desert UVB tube** with UVA for natural vision and behavior
- **Slim aluminum fixture with a polished reflector**, which roughly doubles useful output by directing light downward
- **Mounting clips and screws** for inside-enclosure mounting
- **Power cord with inline switch**

## How to set it up

Mount the fixture inside the enclosure where possible, or directly on top of the mesh at the warm end. A screen top can block 30–50% of UVB, so mount closer if there's mesh in between. Position the tube over the basking area so it covers one-half to two-thirds of the enclosure length, leaving a shaded refuge. Run it with your basking light for 12–14 hours a day on a [digital lighting timer](/shop/heating-lighting/digital-lighting-timer).

Replace the tube every 12 months, because UV output fades long before visible light. Our [UVB lighting explained](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained) article covers distances and UV Index zones in detail, and our [bearded dragon care sheet](/blog/bearded-dragon-care-sheet) shows how UVB fits with basking heat.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a 22 in UVB tube enough for a bearded dragon?

For a juvenile in a 3 ft enclosure, yes. Adults in a 4 × 2 × 2 ft enclosure need a longer tube, around 34 in, to cover enough of the enclosure.

### How far should a T5 HO 12% tube be from my reptile?

As a starting point, about 12–15 in from the reptile's back while basking with the tube inside the enclosure, or closer if mounted above mesh. A UV index meter confirms the actual reading.

### How often should I replace a T5 UVB tube?

Every 12 months, even if it still looks bright. UVB output fades over time and isn't visible to the human eye.

name: Radiant Heat Panel – 80 W
short_description: An 80 W radiant heat panel that mounts flat to the enclosure ceiling and warms animals and surfaces evenly with infrared heat and no light.
long_description:
A radiant heat panel is a flat, ceiling-mounted heater that warms your reptile and the surfaces below it with long-wave infrared, without producing light. This 80 W radiant heat panel has become one of the most popular heat sources for PVC and wooden enclosures, especially for ball pythons, boas and other snakes, because it gives an even, gentle warm zone with no hot bulb to touch.

## Why keepers are switching to heat panels

- **No light:** heat day and night without disturbing your reptile's day–night cycle.
- **Safe to touch:** the panel surface stays far cooler than a ceramic heat emitter, and it's mounted flat to the ceiling where animals can't wrap around it.
- **Even heat:** warms a wide area of the floor and decor rather than one hot spot.
- **Efficient:** heats animals and surfaces rather than the air, which suits closed PVC enclosures.

## Specifications

- **Wattage:** 80 W
- **Size:** about 12 × 24 in (30 × 60 cm), 0.5 in thick
- **Suggested enclosures:** 3 × 2 × 2 ft to 4 × 2 × 2 ft
- **Mounting:** pre-drilled corners and screws for ceiling mounting
- **Cord:** 6 ft cord, compatible with on/off and proportional thermostats

## How to use it

Mount the panel on the ceiling at the warm end of the enclosure. Place the thermostat probe on the warm-side floor or hide, not touching the panel, and use a [proportional thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/proportional-thermostat) for the steadiest temperatures. Heat panels don't provide light or UVB, so pair them with appropriate lighting on a timer. Diurnal basking lizards still need a bright basking light.

For a ball python, aim for a warm-side surface of 88–92°F (31–33°C); our [ball python care guide](/blog/ball-python-care-guide) covers the full gradient, and our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) compares panels, bulbs and ceramic heat emitters.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are radiant heat panels better than ceramic heat emitters?

They're safer to mount inside an enclosure and give more even heat, which is why many snake keepers prefer them. Ceramic emitters are cheaper and fit standard lamp fixtures. The best choice depends on your species and enclosure.

### Do heat panels work in glass terrariums?

They're designed for PVC and wooden enclosures with a solid ceiling. On a mesh-topped glass terrarium, much of the heat escapes upward.

### Do I need a thermostat for a radiant heat panel?

Yes, always. A proportional or on/off thermostat keeps temperatures safe and stable.

name: Terrarium Plant LED Light – Full Spectrum 24 in
short_description: A slim 24 in full-spectrum terrarium plant LED light that keeps live plants growing in bioactive enclosures. Low heat, bright 6500K daylight.
long_description:
A terrarium plant LED light gives live plants the bright, full-spectrum light they need to grow in a bioactive enclosure. Reptile UVB tubes and basking bulbs often aren't enough on their own to keep plants healthy, especially in tall or densely planted vivariums. This 24 in full-spectrum LED bar adds bright 6500K daylight with very little heat, so your plants thrive without changing your temperature gradient.

## Why bioactive enclosures need a plant light

Plants are the backbone of a bioactive setup: they use waste nutrients, hold humidity and give your reptile cover. Without enough light they stretch, yellow and eventually die, leaving bare soil and more maintenance. A dedicated LED makes plant growth predictable, and the bright light also makes your enclosure look natural and vivid.

## Specifications

- **Length:** 24 in (60 cm), suits 24 in and 36 in wide enclosures
- **Spectrum:** full spectrum, 6500K daylight with enhanced red and blue for plant growth
- **Power:** 20 W, very low heat output
- **Mounting:** slim aluminum housing with clips for mesh tops, or brackets for inside PVC enclosures
- **Waterproof rating:** IP65, safe in high-humidity enclosures

## How to use it

Mount the LED across the front of the enclosure, so plants grow toward the viewing side, and run it for 10–12 hours a day with your other lights on a [digital lighting timer](/shop/heating-lighting/digital-lighting-timer). The LED doesn't replace UVB, so keep a [T5 HO UVB 6% tube](/shop/heating-lighting/t5-ho-uvb-6-22in) or a desert tube for your reptile.

Good plants to grow under this light include pothos, bromeliads, peperomia, ferns and fittonia for tropical setups, or haworthia and gasteria for arid ones. Our [bioactive terrarium guide](/blog/how-to-set-up-a-bioactive-terrarium) explains plant choice and setup.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a plant light for a bioactive terrarium?

Usually yes, unless your enclosure is very bright from strong UVB fixtures. Most bioactive keepers add a full-spectrum LED to keep plants healthy.

### Does a plant LED replace UVB for my reptile?

No. LED plant lights don't provide UVB. Your reptile still needs a proper UVB source.

### Will an LED plant light heat my terrarium?

Very little. This 20 W LED runs cool, so it won't noticeably change your temperature gradient.

name: WiFi Reptile Thermostat with App Alerts
short_description: A smart WiFi reptile thermostat with two outlets (dimming and pulse), day/night schedules, temperature logging and phone alerts.
long_description:
A WiFi reptile thermostat lets you check and control your enclosure temperatures from your phone, and warns you the moment something goes wrong. This smart thermostat has two independently controlled outlets, a dimming outlet for basking bulbs and a pulse-proportional outlet for heat panels, ceramic emitters or heat mats, plus day and night schedules, temperature history and push alerts.

## Why keepers are going smart

- **Instant alerts:** get a phone notification if temperatures go too high or too low, or if the power or WiFi drops.
- **Remote control:** adjust set points while you're at work or away.
- **History graphs:** see how temperatures change through the day and night, which makes problems easy to spot.
- **Two zones in one:** run a basking bulb and a night heat source from one unit.

## Specifications

- **Outlet 1:** dimming, for halogen and incandescent bulbs up to 600 W
- **Outlet 2:** pulse-proportional, for ceramic heat emitters, radiant heat panels and heat mats up to 600 W
- **Probes:** two 10 ft probes, one per outlet, plus an optional humidity sensor port
- **Scheduling:** separate day and night set points with sunrise and sunset ramp
- **Safety:** built-in overheat cut-off and a hardware fail-safe that keeps control working if WiFi drops
- **App:** iOS and Android, 2.4 GHz WiFi

## Setting it up

Plug your basking bulb into the dimming outlet with its probe at the basking surface, and your night heater into the pulse outlet with its probe at the warm hide. Set day and night targets for your species, then set alert limits a few degrees outside your normal range. Check readings with an [infrared temperature gun](/shop/care-accessories/infrared-temperature-gun) during the first week.

Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) explains thermostat types and probe placement, and our [preparing your home](/blog/preparing-your-home-for-a-new-reptile) checklist covers testing a new setup.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will the thermostat still work if my WiFi goes down?

Yes. The thermostat controls temperatures on its own; WiFi is only needed for the app and alerts.

### Can I use one outlet for a basking bulb and the other for a heat mat?

Yes. Outlet 1 dims light-emitting bulbs and outlet 2 pulse-controls non-light heaters such as heat mats, panels and ceramic emitters.

### Does it work with 5 GHz WiFi?

It needs a 2.4 GHz network, which most home routers provide alongside 5 GHz.

name: Reptile Heat Cable – 15 ft, 25 W
short_description: A flexible 15 ft reptile heat cable for gentle belly heat under enclosures or along shelves. Waterproof and thermostat ready.
long_description:
A reptile heat cable is a flexible, waterproof heating wire you can route exactly where you want warmth, under an enclosure floor, along the back of a shelf, or zigzagged to create a custom warm area. This 15 ft, 25 W reptile heat cable is a versatile alternative to a fixed heat mat, popular with keepers who run multiple enclosures, quarantine tubs or custom racks.

## Why choose a heat cable

- **Custom shapes:** bend it into any layout to match your enclosure size.
- **Gentle heat:** ideal for belly heat for snakes and geckos.
- **Multiple enclosures:** run one cable under several small tubs on a shelf.
- **Waterproof:** a sealed silicone jacket is safe in humid rooms.

## Specifications

- **Length:** 15 ft (4.5 m)
- **Power:** 25 W
- **Jacket:** waterproof silicone
- **Cord:** 6 ft power lead with plug
- **Includes:** 10 suction cups and adhesive clips for routing

## Safe installation

- **Always use a thermostat.** Place the probe on the enclosure floor directly above the cable. An [on/off thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/on-off-thermostat) or a proportional thermostat works well.
- **Install outside the enclosure,** under the floor or behind a shelf, never inside where animals can dig down to it or chew it.
- **Never cross or overlap the cable,** and keep loops at least 1 in (2.5 cm) apart so heat doesn't build up.
- **Cover only one third to one half of the floor,** so your reptile always has a cooler area.

Belly heat alone doesn't warm the air much, so most enclosures still need an overhead heat source for a full gradient. Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) explains how to combine heat sources safely, and the [Reptile Quarantine Tub](/shop/enclosures/reptile-quarantine-tub) is a common enclosure to use it with.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I bury a heat cable in the substrate?

We don't recommend it. Buried cables can overheat, and animals can dig down to them. Install the cable under the enclosure floor instead.

### Do I need a thermostat for a heat cable?

Yes. Without a thermostat, a heat cable can get hot enough to burn your reptile or damage the enclosure.

### What's the difference between a heat cable and a heat mat?

A heat mat is a fixed rectangle, while a heat cable can be bent into custom shapes and spread across several enclosures.

name: Reptile Heat Tape – 11 in × 10 ft Roll for Racks
short_description: An 11 in × 10 ft roll of reptile heat tape for heating tub-style snake racks. Cut to length; requires connectors and a thermostat.
long_description:
Reptile heat tape is the standard way to heat tub-style racks for snakes and geckos. This 11 in × 10 ft roll of reptile heat tape is thin, flexible and can be cut to the exact length of your rack, giving every tub a consistent warm strip along the back. It's widely used by ball python, hognose and leopard gecko breeders who keep animals in racks.

## How heat tape works

Heat tape runs along the back of each shelf in a rack. Tubs slide in so the back third sits over the tape, creating a warm end while the front of the tub stays cooler. Because every tub gets the same warmth from one long strip, a single thermostat can control a whole rack.

## Specifications

- **Width:** 11 in (28 cm), suits most 15–41 qt tubs
- **Length:** 10 ft (3 m), cut to length at the marked cut lines
- **Power:** about 20 W per linear foot
- **Thickness:** under 1 mm, flat under tubs

## What else you need

- **Heat tape connectors and wire:** clip-on terminals and insulated wire (sold separately) to power each strip.
- **Electrical tape or heat-shrink** to insulate cut ends and connections.
- **A thermostat:** heat tape must always be regulated. A [proportional thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/proportional-thermostat) gives the steadiest temperatures, with the probe taped to the heat tape under a tub.
- **Aluminum tape** to secure the heat tape to the rack shelf.

If you're not comfortable wiring electrical connections, ask a qualified electrician to help.

## Setup tips

Set the thermostat so the floor of each tub above the tape reaches the right surface temperature for your species, for example 88–92°F (31–33°C) for ball pythons and leopard geckos. Check several tubs with an [infrared temperature gun](/shop/care-accessories/infrared-temperature-gun), since temperatures can vary along a rack. Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) covers thermostat choice and probe placement.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use heat tape without a thermostat?

No. Heat tape can reach temperatures that burn animals and damage tubs. Always use a thermostat.

### How do I connect heat tape?

Clip connectors onto the copper strips at the end of the tape, attach insulated wire to a power cord, and insulate every connection. Follow the wiring diagram carefully.

### What size heat tape do I need?

Match the width to your tubs: 11 in tape suits most 15–41 qt tubs. For smaller tubs, narrower tape may be a better fit.

name: Adjustable Reptile Lamp Stand
short_description: An adjustable reptile lamp stand that holds a dome fixture at the perfect height above a terrarium, raising heat lamps off the mesh top.
long_description:
An adjustable reptile lamp stand holds a dome fixture at exactly the right height above your terrarium, instead of resting it directly on the mesh top. Raising the lamp lets you fine-tune basking temperatures, protects the mesh from heat damage and keeps hot fixtures away from curious pets and children. This sturdy stand adjusts in height and reach to fit most glass terrariums and tortoise tables.

## Why use a lamp stand

- **Precise temperatures:** move the lamp up or down to dial in the basking surface temperature without changing bulbs.
- **Protects mesh tops:** a hot dome sitting directly on mesh can warp or discolor it over time.
- **Safer:** keeps fixtures stable and off the lid, reducing the risk of a lamp being knocked over.
- **Open-top enclosures:** essential for tortoise tables and other enclosures without a mesh top to rest a lamp on.

## Specifications

- **Height:** adjustable from 14 to 27 in (36–69 cm)
- **Arm reach:** 8 in (20 cm) horizontal arm with a swivel hook
- **Base:** weighted steel base with non-slip pads
- **Compatible with:** clamp lamps and dome fixtures up to 8.5 in, including our [deep dome lamp fixture](/shop/heating-lighting/deep-dome-lamp-fixture)
- **Finish:** heat-resistant black powder coat

## How to use it

Place the stand beside the warm end of the enclosure and hang the dome from the hook, with the reflector pointing straight down over the basking spot. Adjust the height while checking the basking surface with an infrared thermometer until it's in range for your species, then tighten the knobs. For tortoise tables, combine the stand with a [mercury vapor bulb](/shop/heating-lighting/mercury-vapor-bulb-100w) or a halogen basking bulb plus a separate UVB source.

Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) explains how lamp distance affects basking temperatures.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will a lamp stand fit my terrarium?

It fits most glass terrariums and tortoise tables up to about 24 in tall when the lamp needs to sit just above the top. Check the height range against your enclosure before buying.

### Can I use a lamp stand with a UVB tube?

It's designed for dome fixtures and clamp lamps. Linear UVB tube fixtures are best mounted on or inside the enclosure.

### How high should my heat lamp be?

High enough that the basking surface reaches your species' target temperature, measured with an infrared thermometer. Start higher and lower the lamp gradually.
